faq: Which websites can you work with?
Any public site that your users visit and that allows extensions to run. We do not build scripts that break a site's terms, scrape private data for resale or bypass logins.
What happens when a website changes its layout?
Scripts that depend on page structure can break. Premium adds fallback selectors to reduce that, and our maintenance service can handle repairs after later site changes.
Will it slow the pages my users visit?
We keep scripts small, run them only on matching pages and avoid heavy loops. On Premium we also check performance on a busy page and fix anything that slows it.
Does it read my users' private page content?
Only what the feature needs, and only on the sites you list. We avoid sending page content anywhere unless the feature requires it, and we explain it for your privacy policy.

desc:
Browser extension content scripts from Ecom Swift LLC read or change the pages your users visit, such as adding a button or reading a price, while staying fast, narrowly scoped and respectful of user privacy.

## What are content scripts in a browser extension?

Content scripts are the files of an extension that run inside a web page rather than in the extension's own popup or background worker. They can read the page's text, find elements, add buttons, change styles and send messages back to the rest of the extension. They run in an isolated environment, so they can touch the page without sharing variables with the site's own code.

Because they run on websites you do not control, content scripts need extra care. A careless one slows the page, breaks the site or reads more than it should.

## Why content scripts need careful engineering

The page belongs to someone else, and it can change at any time. A script that works today may fail next month when the site renames a class or moves a button. A script that runs on every address in the browser can also drag down every tab the user opens.

Good content scripts do the opposite. They match only named pages, wait for elements that load late and fail quietly when something is missing. Users never notice them, which is the goal. Reviewers at the store also look at how much page access an extension requests, so a narrow match list builds trust as well as speed.

## What well-made content scripts include

- Match patterns limited to the exact sites and paths you name.
- Run timing chosen so the script starts when the page is ready, not before.
- Handling for elements that appear after the first load.
- Support for sites that change the page without reloading, common in single-page apps.
- Page styles kept isolated, so your button does not inherit the site's look.
- Messages between the script and your popup or background worker.
- Fallback selectors, so one renamed class does not break the feature.
- Cleanup of listeners and observers, to avoid memory leaks.
- A small test page that you can reuse after each change.
- A plain-language note on why each permission is requested.

## How we approach the work

We begin on the real pages you want to support. We inspect how each site builds the elements you care about and pick selectors that are stable rather than fragile. Then we write the script, load it as an unpacked extension and test across normal pages, slow connections and pages with unusual layouts.

The packages scale with the number of sites. Basic covers one script on one site. Standard handles several sites or page types, two-way messages with your popup and late-loading content. Premium adds fallback selectors, single-page navigation, a performance check on heavy pages, a reusable test page and a period of fixes after handover.

We tell you plainly which sites are risky to rely on, for example pages behind a login or pages that change their markup often.

## Do and avoid with content scripts

**Do:**
- Name the exact pages where the script should run.
- Keep reads limited to the elements the feature needs.
- Use your own styles inside an isolated container.
- Check the script again after any big change on the target site.
- Explain to users what the script does on their pages.

**Avoid:**
- Matching every website when you only need one.
- Reading form fields, passwords or private messages.
- Polling the page on a tight timer instead of watching for changes.
- Copying a site's styles by guessing its class names.
- Assuming a site will never change its layout.

## Who this is for

It suits a shopper tool that adds a price tracker next to product listings. It suits a recruiter or sales team that wants a button on a professional site to save a contact to their system. And it suits a company that wants an accessibility helper that adjusts reading size on its own web app.

## What we need from you

Send the web addresses where the script should work, a short description of what it should add or change, and screenshots if you have a design in mind. Tell us whether the pages require a login so we can plan testing.

We never need your passwords. If a page requires an account, a test account that you create is enough, or you can share screen recordings of the flow. We reply with a short plan before we write any code.
